name: Silk (SS)
description: The Spider Cave's set silk, drawn from above like everything else on that floor and built in the order a spider builds one: a frame slung between eight anchor points, no two of them the same distance out, sixteen radii that each stop ON a frame line rather than in mid-air, a hub with a free zone round it the spider keeps clear to turn in, and then one capture thread wound outward — drawn as the straight chords it is really made of, which is why a web is a polygon spiral and not a stack of circles. Beaded with glue along the sticky courses, broken through in three places with the cut ends curled back on the radii that held, and behind all of it the ghost of an older web at another angle. Caught in it: a wing, a husk, a leg and a scatter of dew. Cold white (`$silent`) on cave stone, because silk is the one thing down there brighter than anything alive. `torn` is the state after somebody has walked through it; `sheet` is the same patch spun by something that does not build orbs — a tangled mat whose every line runs home to a funnel — and `sheet_torn` is that walked through. The game scales all four to whatever radius the patch rolled.

torn.description: Walked through: the sticky spiral is mostly gone, its beads with it, and what is left hangs off the frame and the radii — the only parts built to hold anything. Still silk; it just does not hold you.

sheet.description: A funnel-weaver's mat: no hub, no radii, no spiral — layered tangle with drag lines running back to a throat, so a step anywhere on it is felt at home. Same drag, nothing in common to look at.

sheet_torn.description: The mat, walked through: the tangle pulled open, the drag lines snapped back, the funnel's rim collapsed and the throat under it showing.
